text:
alice: Kicking off FP8 canary on H100/L40S pools. After warmup we see regular 2-3x tail latency spikes on generation workloads (~2k tokens). Dumped a perf profile, sharing below.

ben: Can you paste the kernel selector snapshot? suspect fallback to int8 kernels when seq_len patterns change.

alice: Pasted selector/log snippet from the canary node:```
[2026-07-12 14:03:21] selector: chosen_kernel=fp8_matmul_fwd_v2, heuristics=seq<64,temp_cache=enabled
[2026-07-12 14:03:24] selector: chosen_kernel=int8_gemm_small for layer=9, seq=30
[2026-07-12 14:03:24] transformer_engine: quant_mode=automatic, fallback_margin=0.12
[2026-07-12 14:03:28] kv_cache: eviction=on, cache_hits=0.82 -> 0.47 after warmup
```

chandra: Interesting — looks like small-seq kernel switching mid-request. That will blow up latency because we rebind kernels and the TE call path isn't prewarmed. Also KV eviction drop to 47% means a ton of recompute.

maria: Any change when forcing single kernel family? try `--force-kernel=fp8_matmul_fwd_v2` on a test pod. If latency stabilizes, kernel switch is root cause.

alice: Ran a quick A/B:
- A: default selector -> 2.4x tail spikes, p50=32ms p95=210ms p99=480ms
- B: forced `fp8_matmul_fwd_v2` -> p50=30ms p95=84ms p99=120ms
So big improvement when we avoid on-the-fly switching.

zach: That narrows it. But why is selector choosing int8_gemm_small? workload has mixed prompt lengths with many short completions. Selector heuristic uses seq histogram to pick kernel per-layer. When distribution shifts during a request (prefix+generated tokens), we can flip.

chandra: Also thread: transformer engine's `quant_mode=automatic` performs calibration/scale updates during warmup. If calibration changes mid-request, kernel metadata changes and we hit path that triggers a kernel graph rebuild. Those rebuilds are heavy on H100 in our TE build.

ben: Can we delay calibration to prewarm window only? or pin calibration to node startup. If calibration is stable after N steps, prevent runtime updates for in-flight sessions.

alice: I tried `TE_CALIBRATION_LOCK=1` on canary for 30m run: no rebuilds observed, KV cache hit stayed >0.8, tail latency dropped to near baseline. But that doesn't solve long-term accuracy concerns.

maria: We should investigate batching heuristics too. Current dynamic batching groups mixed lengths aggressively which increases kernel-switch probability. Maybe split batches by seq-length buckets before scheduling.

zach: Agreed. Proposed short-term mitigations: 1) force fp8 kernel family for the canary tier, 2) pin calibration to startup, 3) add seq-bucketing in batching service. Long-term: make selector aware of in-flight generation dynamics and prefer stable kernels for multi-call requests.

perf-bot: perf snapshot uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/fp8-canary/1899876543/profile.tar.gz (flamegraphs + kernel traces).

chandra: Next steps I can take: instrument selector to emit `decision_reason` and `predicted_switch_cost` for each candidate; add a cheap estimate of kernel rebind cost to heuristics. Will also add a metric for "kernel_switches_per_request." 

alice: Thanks. I'll schedule a canary with `--force-kernel` and `TE_CALIBRATION_LOCK=1` for the next 2 hours and run the regression harness. If good, roll these as temporary flags for all H100/L40S until we implement selector changes.

ben: One more data point: on L40S we saw less rebuild penalty (lower SPM) but KV warming still causes throughput jitter. Might be a memory allocator interaction causing KV evictions when TE reallocs scratch buffers during kernel swap. Add to investigation.

maria: I'll prototype seq-bucketing in the batcher. If we separate short/long queues, we keep kernel footprints stable. Could be a 10-20% throughput cost but big tail reduction.

alice: Great. Recording action items: 
- chandra: telemetry + `kernel_switches_per_request` + selector decision_reason (ETA next week)
- maria: seq-bucketing prototype (ETA 3 days)
- ben: test L40S allocator interplay (ETA 2 days)
- zach: hold canary force-kernel + calibration lock (running now)

alice: Thanks all :thumbsup: any objections to making the force-kernel/calibration-lock a temporary config across the canary fleet?

ben: nope, sounds good. Keep perf-bot reporting.

maria: no objections. Will post a short write-up when prototype is in PR.

zach: I'll keep an eye on SLOs and rollback if anything odd shows up.
